messages:
devin: Quick heads up — after yesterday's retry change I'm seeing duplicate billing events for the same user requests. tagging @maria @chris to loop you in. sample below.

chris: ugh. can you paste a minimal example of the dupes? request_id / event_id differences? :thinking:

devin: sure. here's two events we got within 2s for the same call:
```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_01Gabc",
  "request_id": "req_9f2b",
  "customer_id": "org_42",
  "model": "redwood-3b",
  "tokens": 128,
  "status": "ok",
  "producer_version": "v2-retry"
}
{
  "event_id": "evt_01Gabd",
  "request_id": "req_9f2b",
  "customer_id": "org_42",
  "model": "redwood-3b",
  "tokens": 128,
  "status": "ok",
  "producer_version": "v2-retry"
}
```
Both look identical except event_id. producer retried the send but included same request_id. our consumer currently emits both as billable events.

maria: hmm. we should have dedupe based on (customer_id, request_id) at the billing stage. but need to think about cross-partition keys — we shard by customer_id currently so ok. also what's the ingestion guarantee? exactly-once?

devin: ingestion is at-least-once (kafka). no producer-side idempotent topic. we rely on consumer dedupe right now.

sylvia: two levers: 1) enforce producer-side idempotency (sidecar/SDK writes to idempotent topic or sets canonical_request_id) 2) consumer dedupe store (redis/rocksdb) keyed by (customer_id, request_id, model). tradeoffs: producer approach is cleaner but requires rollouts across many clients; consumer approach centralizes logic but needs durable dedupe store and TTL.

alex: also consider auditability. if we drop duplicates at consumer without storing the raw duplicate, we lose the original event for forensic audits/backfills. we should keep a raw_events archive (S3) and mark which event_id was accepted as the canonical one.

chris: agreed. propose: write raw events to cold storage first (compressed), then push an enriched canonical_event to billing topic. enrichment service picks canonical_request_id and emits single billing record. that lets replays/backfills re-run enrichment.

maria: timeline note: late-arriving attribution (e.g., post-hoc model attribution or rerank) means we need to be able to update billing records or emit correction events. design for corrections rather than mutating historical bills. :+1:

devin: correction events are fine. they have to be idempotent too. maybe add a field `correction_of: <event_id>` and `correction_type: add|subtract|replace`.

sylvia: performance question: dedupe lookup per event adds latency. we can batch dedupe checks for windows and use a write-through compaction table (Kafka compacted topic keyed by (customer_id, request_id)) to cheaply check membership. downside: compaction latency and eventual consistency during rollouts.

chris: another angle: token attribution granularity. do we bill per-request (sum tokens across subcalls) or per-subcall? many clients do multi-model pipelines (prompt -> rerank -> refine). we need attribution mapping back to top-level usage and to feature flags. schema idea:
```json
{
  "canonical_event": true,
  "request_id": "req_9f2b",
  "root_session_id": "sess_77",
  "calls": [
    {"call_id":"call_a","model":"redwood-3b","tokens":100},
    {"call_id":"call_b","model":"reranker-1","tokens":28}
  ],
  "total_tokens":128
}
```
This lets downstream charge per-model and also roll up.

alex: for billing accuracy we might need token-level provenance for expensive prompts (store hash of prompt + call_id) so we can re-run evals if customers dispute. but that's heavy. maybe only keep hashes and sampling of full payloads for a short window.

maria: action items: (1) add `canonical_request_id` producer opt-in header + SDK bump (low-effort) (2) build consumer dedupe as fallback with TTL 30d and compacted index topic (3) store raw_events to cold S3 with partition by date/customer (4) define correction event schema and handling flow (5) add QA/backfill runbook.

devin: created a short RFC + proposed schema changes in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/412 (metering-bot created).

metering-bot: PR #412 opened by devin: "dedupe/enrichment: canonical_request_id + correction events + raw archive flow" — reviewers: @maria @chris @sylvia

chris: will review today. rough +1 on design, want to prototype compaction topic latency first.

sylvia: I'll sketch the dedupe store design (redis vs rocksdb vs compacted kafka) and post numbers tomorrow.

maria: thanks all. let's sync in the platform cadence tomorrow. if anyone hits duplicates in the wild, drop examples here. :wave:
